entityDescription:
Safe passage for your mission.
 
Testspring is a one-stop shop for space systems verification and validation. We plan and execute full qualification campaigns under a single contract through:
1. Our Orbital TestLabs (in-orbit test platforms)
2. Our network of established test facilities and analog sites
3. Simulation environments.
 
We also support clients on a modular basis: running a single test, providing qualified testers, or taking on particular V&V tasks within a larger programme.
 
Whether you need the full campaign or a single test, you get one point of contact instead of five.
 
Our campaigns support clients across the full maturity range, from TRL 3 breadboard validation to TRL 9. We structure our work around the ECSS framework, including: ECSS-E-ST-10-02 (Verification), ECSS-E-ST-10-03 (Testing), ECSS-E-ST-40 (Software engineering), and ECSS-Q-ST-80 (Software product assurance).
 
We are an ideal partner for:
1. Primes qualifying new technology
2. Startups seeking flight heritage for software components
3. Developers of robotics, rovers, payloads, and autonomy systems who need to verify concepts, procedures, and designs before committing to a full mission
We accommodate hardware payloads on a case-by-case basis.
 
We help you reduce:
1. Time-to-orbit
2. Risk
3. Programme costs.
 
You find failures before they become expensive, uncover unknowns that pose a risk to a mission, and arrive at launch with systems and software that have already flown.
 
Our mission:
To democratise access to space by improving accessibility and reducing the overall cost of getting there. We want to provide a unified platform for all European Space Sector participants, bridging the gap between well-established businesses and new space initiatives.

entityDescription:
B2Space is a UK-based aerospace company headquartered in Newport, Wales, developing and operating high-altitude stratospheric platforms for near-space testing, Earth observation, surveillance, communications, and future launch applications.
Founded with the long-term ambition of becoming the first UK satellite launch company using the “rockoon” concept — where a stratospheric balloon lifts a launch platform to near-space altitude before deploying a rocket — B2Space has progressively built a strong commercial and technical foundation around reusable stratospheric systems, balloon operations, mission control, payload integration, and high-altitude flight services.
Today, B2Space operates across three complementary business lines.
The first is Near Space Testing, originally developed with the support of ESA BIC UK. This service enables companies, universities, research organisations, and public institutions to test and validate technologies, sensors, materials, payloads, communications systems, and mission concepts in the stratosphere. These flights provide access to a near-space environment with low pressure, low temperature, high radiation exposure, and operational conditions relevant to space missions, helping customers accelerate technology development and increase Technology Readiness Levels at a significantly lower cost than orbital demonstration.
The second business line is the development and operation of High Altitude Pseudo-Satellite platforms, including stratospheric balloons, MicroHABS systems, and other high-altitude assets. These platforms can support applications such as Earth observation, environmental monitoring, wildfire detection, surveillance, communications, intelligence gathering, and rapid-response missions. B2Space’s approach combines flexible deployment, low operating cost, payload adaptability, and the ability to provide persistent or repeated coverage from the stratosphere.
The third area remains B2Space’s long-term rockoon launch system, which builds on the company’s expertise in high-altitude operations, autonomous flight systems, airborne launch architectures, and stratospheric platform development. While the company’s commercial activity today is focused on near-space testing and HAPS services, the rockoon programme continues to form part of B2Space’s strategic roadmap toward affordable and responsive access to space.
B2Space has developed substantial operational heritage, having performed numerous stratospheric flights with payloads ranging from small experimental systems to large and complex platforms. The company has delivered services and systems to commercial, institutional, defence, and space-sector customers, including work related to technology validation, high-altitude operations, Earth observation, and HAPS development.
To date, B2Space has secured several million euros in private equity, grant funding, and commercial revenues, and has generated multi-million-euro B2B sales through its high-altitude services and technology programmes. This commercial traction, combined with its operational experience and growing portfolio of stratospheric platforms, positions B2Space as one of the leading European companies in high-altitude balloon and HAPS operations.

entityDescription: The Institute is dedicated to a broad portfolio of research and education, ranging from fundamental questions concerning symmetries and interactions in nuclear and particle physics, neutron physics, atomic physics, quantum physics and quantum optics to radiation physics and reactor technology. Its activities also include applied research in areas such as environmental analysis, radiation protection and testing the radiation resistance of modern materials. A central facility of the Institute is the TRIGA Mark II research reactor, together with the associated teaching and laboratory facilities, which enable research and teaching involving radioactive substances and ionizing radiation. In this context, the Institute also makes an important contribution to the training and education of experts from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). At present, the Institute's staff comprises approximately 32 scientific employees (18 in permanent positions and 14 on six-year contracts) and 29 non-scientific employees. In addition, around 70 project staff are financed through third-party funding. Their contribution to the Institute's research and teaching activities has grown continuously in recent years. Furthermore, approximately 70 students are currently working on their bachelor's theses, diploma theses or doctoral dissertations at the Institute. The teaching offered by the Institute covers all of its research areas and is integrated into the curricula of the Faculty of Physics.

Company description: The National Biodiversity Future Center (NBFC) focuses on the Mediterranean region, considered a biodiversity hotspot, in order to address global challenges related to the following:
-Knowledge and protection of Italian biodiversity;

The NBFC is therefore proposed as a national and international reference for generating knowledge and value from biodiversity and transferring them to the territory with the aim of implementing ecosystem services, promoting the well-being of people and generating social and environmental economic value for society.

eXact lab specialises in scientific computing, high-performance computing (HPC), scientific software development, and data infrastructure. Its staff come almost entirely from scientific and research backgrounds — nearly half hold a PhD in Physics, Mathematics, Geophysics, or Civil Engineering — giving the company the technical depth to operate at the intersection of research and engineering. software design and optimisation for large-scale data processing;

HPC infrastructure design, deployment, and management;

software performance optimisation;

AI and machine learning for scientific and industrial applications;

training in technologies related to the activities above.

The company is organised in two main business units. The Operations BU covers provisioning, administration, and management of HPC infrastructure. The Development BU covers all software development activities and is divided into Data Science and HPC sub-units. As is typical of a SME, boundaries between units are intentionally permeable: project teams are cross-disciplinary and staff contribute across the full stack, so that expertise in HPC, data engineering, and scientific software is distributed rather than siloed.

eXact lab has extensive experience across the full value chain of Earth Observation data: from devising and deploying the compute-intensive processing pipelines that turn raw sensor data into scientific products, to designing and managing the data infrastructure that makes those products discoverable and accessible, to building the programmatic interfaces that end users rely on in operational workflows. This end-to-end familiarity — spanning production, distribution, and use of EO data — is directly relevant to a contract requiring user-driven maintenance and development of a key component of the Copernicus Marine Service ecosystem such as the toolbox.

In the field of civil engineering, our experience extends to the specialized design of underground spaces and subsurface structures, as well as large-scale retaining structures. Our tunnelling expertise encompasses various methodologies, including the Shotcrete Lining (SCL), Tunnel Boring Machine (TBM) technology, and Cut-and-Cover techniques, along with deep foundation systems and complex soil-structure interaction analysis.
We utilize advanced Finite Element Method (FEM) software to model non-linear structural behaviour and optimize material efficiency in challenging subterranean environments. Balogh Statikus Iroda Kft. prioritizes analytical accuracy and structural safety, delivering engineering solutions that meet the rigorous technical demands of both the European and American construction markets.

As part of the national STEAM Center Network, it serves as a dynamic bridge between research, education, and industry. As a department of one of Central and Eastern Europe’s oldest and most prestigious universities, the Centre builds on Vilnius University's robust research infrastructure. Eight cutting-edge laboratories — Robotics, Visual Programming, Engineering, Fabrication, Light (Laser) Technologies, Physics and Astronomy, Life Sciences, and Chemistry — empower students aged 13–19 to engage in hands-on scientific exploration, creative problem-solving, and innovation.

Research-driven evaluation of STEAM learning effectiveness.

By aligning with national and European priorities, the Vilnius University Methodical STEAM Education Centre plays a vital role in advancing high-quality, inclusive education and shaping the next generation of scientists, engineers, and innovators.

entityDescription: Space42 Europe Srls - hereafter Space42 - is an Italian start-up company, founded in 2019, by a network of professional scientific explainers with more than 12 years of experience in communicating science and technology-related topics to the public. Space42 designs multimedia materials, presentations, hands-on workshops for young students, participates in science-themed public events on its own behalf or in support of national and international scientific entities. All proposed scientific activities and laboratories are indeed designed and implemented by Space42 experts and coordinated, during the event, by scientific explainers directly provided by the company. All materials needed for workshops are also prepared by the team and made available to the students during the activities. Each event is run by Space42 professionals, eventually supported by volunteers provided by partner institutions. Space42 has collaborations with the European Space Agency, the Italian Space Agency, the Distretto Tecnologico Aerospaziale, Il Cielo Itinerante, Asia Onlus, Camera di Commercio di Roma, Parmalat, Frascati Scienza, Unicef and ENEL for the organization of scientific events, festivals and tours throughout Italy addressed to young generations, with the aim of disseminating Space and Science in general and promoting the study of STEM disciplines. In particular, the network collaborates with the European Space Agency since 2017, for the organization of a wide variety of dissemination events in Italy and in Europe. As such, Space42 is responsible for all visits to the ESA - ESRIN Italian establishment for primary and secondary schools. On behalf of the Agency, Space42 participates in major scientific events and festivals in Italy and abroad. The group collaborated with the Italian Space Agency as well, in the years 2018, 2019 to plan, manage and coordinate the ASI one-week Open Days and the European Researchers Night in 2022. In 2020, 2021 and 2022 Space42 worked with Il Cielo Itinerante organization bringing scientific labs throughout Italy, with a special focus on educationally disadvantaged areas. The 2022 tour covered 45 dates throughout the country.

entityDescription: TSI is a Spanish engineering company with more than four decades of experience in noise and vibration control, structural dynamics and condition monitoring.
